key_insight: YSZ and intumescent thermal barrier coatings delayed fire-induced buckling and improved post-fire strength retention in thin-walled cold-formed steel, with intumescent coating performing marginally better.
engineering_relevance: These coatings offer potentially lightweight fire protection for cold-formed steel without bulky gypsum encasement.
method: Tested S355 lipped channels (150 × 50 × 2 mm) under ISO-834 fire exposure: 10 specimens each for uncoated, plasma-sprayed YSZ and epoxy-based intumescent groups.
Tracked buckling and temperature using LVDTs and thermocouples; measured post-fire tensile properties using ASTM E8 tests.
Reproduced behaviour with nonlinear ABAQUS models and numerically explored a functionally graded coating.
evidence_signal: Across the three experimental groups, both coatings outperformed uncoated steel, but the abstract provides no numerical effect sizes.
watch_item: The functionally graded coating remains experimentally unvalidated, and any changes to Eurocode 3 reduction factors require broader validation.
paper_title: Advancing cold-formed steel with thermal barrier coatings: buckling and fire resistance behaviours
